slides.eyebrow: Here's the truth about rate locks
slides.sub: 3 things to check. Start with your Loan Estimate.
slides.source: CFPB, What's a lock-in or a rate lock (reviewed May 2023)

slides.label: COMMON LOCK PERIODS
slides.body: Mortgage rates can change daily, sometimes hourly. Locks usually run 30, 45 or 60 days, sometimes longer. Close in time and your rate holds, if your application doesn't change.
slides.source: CFPB, What's a lock-in or a rate lock (reviewed May 2023)

slides.title: Check page 1 of your Loan Estimate
slides.body: The Rate Lock line at the top says Yes or No. If it's locked, it shows the date and time the lock ends. Some lenders lock with the Loan Estimate. Some don't.
slides.source: CFPB Loan Estimate guide (2017); CFPB Loan Estimate page (Oct. 2025)

slides.title: A lock isn't a freeze
slides.body: If your loan amount, credit score or verified income changes, your locked rate can change too. So can a new loan type, down payment or appraisal value.
slides.source: CFPB, What's a lock-in or a rate lock (reviewed May 2023)

slides.title: Ask before you lock
slides.body: What happens if closing runs late and the lock ends? Extending it can be expensive. Ask about any lock fee too. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
slides.source: CFPB (2023); Federal Reserve, A Consumer's Guide to Mortgage Lock-Ins

caption:
Here's the truth about rate locks: your locked rate can still change before closing. Rates can change daily, sometimes hourly, and a lock usually runs 30, 45 or 60 days, sometimes longer.

Check the top of page 1 of your Loan Estimate to see if your rate is locked and when the lock ends. A change in your loan amount, credit score or verified income can still change it.

Ask what happens if closing runs late. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
